To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the particle size of aerosolized drugs is a key determinant for their deposition in different regions in the respiratory tract, and that the breathing pattern of patients has a significant impact on the deposition.
particle size is the most important parameter influencing the deposition in the respiratory tract.

1) the particle size of an aerosol is the most important parameter for the distribution of an aerosol in the respiratory tract, 2) the breathing pattern of a patient is the most important determinant of the distribution of an inhaled aerosol and 3) the inhalation device influences the particle size and the distribution of an inhalation aerosol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of inhalation devices, which allow an efficient drug delivery.
the development of new aerosol devices and the optimization of existing inhalation systems.

the following topics: (i) the influence of particle size and the breathing parameters on the aerosol deposition in healthy and diseased lungs, (ii) the influence of aerosol properties on the drug deposition in the lung, (iii) the development of a model for the simulation of drug transport in the respiratory tract and (iv) the development of new inhalation devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aerosol therapy in asthma is effective and safe.
the particle size of the inhaled drug has the highest impact on the deposition in different lung regions.
the aerosol therapy is an effective treatment option, but it requires the knowledge and experience of the treating physician.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inhaled bronchodilators and corticoids should be in a particle size of 1-5 micrometers.
the aerosol therapy in asthma patients should be performed with an aerosol with a mass median particle diameter (MMPD) of 5-7 μm.
the inhalation technique should be taught to the patients and the use of the inhalation device should be controlled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are a number of different factors which can influence the effectiveness of aerosol therapy.
the aerosol deposition in the lung is highly dependent on the breathing pattern and that it is possible to increase the deposition in the lungs by changing the breathing pattern.

the use of a nebulizer is more effective than a metered-dose inhaler in terms of drug delivery and the amount of drug reaching the lungs, and the use of a spacer is more effective than using a metered-dos inhaler alone.
